doc.title: Frank Foster and Bill Hughes interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Schenectady, New York, March 28, 1995

title: Foster arrives late in Chicago
summary: Foster misses the first half of a Birdland show but walks on in time for his break on Dinner with Friends.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: There was a time in Chicago when we played, it was a Birdland show, we played at the opera house, and the concert started at 8:00. And I’d had company that afternoon at the hotel, and at 8:00 I was just waking up, and the band was playing, no Frank Foster. So I hurriedly got dressed and called a taxi down to the theater, and I had got there just in time to miss the first half. So I walked in after the intermission was over, and hurriedly got my horn out. In the meantime, the first song after intermission was a song of Neal Hefti’s called “Dinner with Friends” that featured a solo break. Like I had a two measure break, and into the solo. A break is where the horn player or soloist is all by him or herself, and the rhythm section lays out, and then they start back at the beginning of the solo. So Frank Wess was getting prepared to take my solo, ‘cause ostensibly I hadn’t shown yet. And so when it came to this part in the song, it was going to be just before the break and sort of an interlude. [scats] And as Frank Wess was standing up ready to play, here I come walking on stage just in time to make the break.
Yeah, I took it — it was my solo. So before they cursed me out, they laughed. Then then cursed me out.
